properties.name: Río Verde
properties.desc: Largest tributary near Guadalajara; joins the Santiago at the bottom of the Barranca de Huentitán. El Zapotillo dam on this river now sends water to the metro area.

properties.name: Río Grande de Santiago
properties.desc: Leaves Lake Chapala at Ocotlán and runs north-west through the El Salto industrial corridor, past Guadalajara in the Barranca de Huentitán, through four hydro dams to the Pacific near San Blas, Nayarit. Its Jalisco reach is among the most polluted rivers in Mexico.
properties.rows: [["Length","562 km (CONAGUA)"],["Mean natural runoff","7,349 hm³/yr (≈233 m³/s)"],["Basin","76,277 km²"]]

properties.name: Río Juchipila
properties.desc: Partly piped (culvert segments through Zapopan/Colomos); old Presa de Atemajac (Zoquipan) dam at 20.7126,-103.3707. Into the Rio Santiago in the Barranca de Huentitan. OSM line ends at 20.7434,-103.3273 (1.8 km short of the river); nearest channel point 20.7533,-103.3132.

properties.name: Río Atemajac
properties.desc: Partly piped (culvert segments through Zapopan/Colomos); old Presa de Atemajac (Zoquipan) dam at 20.7126,-103.3707. Into the Rio Santiago in the Barranca de Huentitan. OSM line ends at 20.7434,-103.3273 (1.8 km short of the river); nearest channel point 20.7533,-103.3132.

properties.name: Canal Las Pintas
properties.desc: Open canal that drains south Guadalajara/Tlaquepaque towards Arroyo El Ahogado and then the Santiago above the Juanacatlán falls.

properties.name: Río Lerma
properties.desc: Drains the industrial Bajío (Estado de México, Querétaro, Guanajuato, Michoacán) and is Chapala’s main inflow. It brings municipal, industrial and agricultural waste into the lake that supplies most of Guadalajara’s water.

properties.name: Río San Juan de Dios
properties.desc: Piped (embovedado) from 1909; runs under Calzada Independencia; open channel in the median of Av. Normalistas; rises at Parque Agua Azul. North to the Periferico at the Guadalajara/Zapopan limit, then joins the Rio Atemajac (OSM shows it joining Atemajac at ~20.728,-103.331) before entering the barranca.

properties.name: Río Zula
properties.kind: Tributary · joins the Santiago at Ocotlán
properties.desc: Basin 1215 Río Zula is in deficit (−17.448 hm³/yr, DOF 2020). Carries Ocotlán–Arandas agro-industrial waste into the first km of the Santiago.
